title: Agency nurse spend has tripled at Larchmere Regional Medical Center's nursing division

organization.size: 412 licensed beds, approx. 3,100 staff; nursing division of 18 inpatient units with 760 permanent RNs (budgeted 890 RN FTE) at 2026-09-30

presentingRequest: Our agency nurse bill has tripled in two years and it is now the single largest overrun in the hospital budget. This is a market problem: regional nurse wages have gone through the roof, and since St. Brennan's opened in March they have been poaching our people. We tried the orientation-coordinator experiment on 4 West last autumn and resignations did not move, so we are not going down that road again. The board has approved, in principle, a $15,000 sign-on bonus to out-hire St. Brennan's in FY2027, funded within the nursing budget as the CFO has proposed. We want your help designing the bonus terms and the recruitment campaign so we can get agency spend down by the end of next year. - Dr. Miriam Osei, Chief Nursing Officer

evidence.text: 'Agency spend was $6.2 million in 2024 and $18.9 million over the last twelve months. Agency rates have exploded with the regional wage market, and St. Brennan's has been taking our nurses since it opened. We cannot fix a market problem from the inside, so we have to pay to win the hiring war. On 4 West we put in a dedicated orientation coordinator in October 2025 and capped charge shifts; I looked at the numbers at the end of Q1 2026 and 4 West lost four nurses that quarter, exactly as before. It did not work, and it cost us an educator FTE.'

evidence.source: Finance department agency-cost analysis (prepared by the Director of Financial Planning, 2026-10-20)
evidence.text: Agency RN hours billed: calendar 2024: 63,200 hours at an average billed rate of $98.10/hour ($6.20M); calendar 2025: 116,600 hours at $101.20/hour ($11.80M); trailing twelve months Oct 2025-Sep 2026: 162,900 hours at $116.00/hour ($18.90M). Quarterly agency hours: Q1 2024 13,900; Q4 2024 17,800; Q4 2025 34,900; Q3 2026 44,300. Decomposition of the $12.7M increase from 2024 to TTM: volume effect (TTM hours at the 2024 rate) $9.78M, about 77%; rate effect $2.92M, about 23%. The master agency contract (Vantage Clinical Staffing, renewal due 2027-01-01) contains an escalator clause that adjusts bill rates each January by the change in the state RN median wage index; the index rose 9.4% for 2025 and 7.9% for 2026, and billed base rates moved by exactly those percentages. Two other vendors on the regional purchasing framework quoted rates 6-8% below Vantage's current rates for the same credentialing requirements.

evidence.source: HR workforce dashboard, RN vacancy and voluntary resignations by quarter, Q1 2024-Q3 2026 (HRIS export, 2026-10-22)
evidence.text: RN vacancy rate (budgeted FTE unfilled), end of quarter: Q1 2024 6.1%; Q2 2024 6.4%; Q3 2024 7.3%; Q4 2024 8.6%; Q1 2025 9.8%; Q2 2025 10.9%; Q3 2025 11.7%; Q4 2025 12.6%; Q1 2026 13.5%; Q2 2026 14.4%; Q3 2026 14.8%. Voluntary RN resignations per quarter: Q1 2024 17; Q2 2024 18; Q3 2024 24; Q4 2024 27; Q1 2025 31; Q2 2025 33; Q3 2025 38; Q4 2025 41; Q1 2026 44; Q2 2026 47; Q3 2026 45. The rate at which vacancies are filled with external hires has been roughly flat at 26-34 RN hires per quarter throughout.

evidence.source: Nursing policy NUR-114 'Supplemental and agency staff' (rev. 2023-06; current)
evidence.text: Agency RNs may not serve as charge nurse, preceptor, or rapid-response nurse. Each agency RN on first assignment to a unit completes two buddy-orientation shifts paired with a permanent RN, who carries a reduced assignment for those shifts. Charge duties are to be rotated among charge-qualified permanent RNs. Standard agency assignment length is 13 weeks. Of the 760 permanent RNs at 2026-09-30, 212 are charge-qualified and 248 are preceptor-qualified (the groups overlap heavily).

evidence.source: Staffing and scheduling system extract (Nurse Staffing Office, 2026-10-24)
evidence.text: Charge shifts per charge-qualified permanent RN per month: Q1 2024 2.1; Q4 2024 2.7; Q4 2025 3.9; Q3 2026 4.6. Agency buddy-orientation shifts worked by permanent RNs: 2024 1,130; TTM Oct 2025-Sep 2026 3,410. By unit, Q3 2026: in the 7 units where agency nurses worked more than 20% of RN hours, charge-qualified permanent RNs averaged 5.8 charge plus buddy-orientation shifts per month; in the 6 units below 10% agency hours, they averaged 2.4. The increase in charge and orientation shifts on each unit followed, rather than preceded, the increase in that unit's agency share in every one of the 7 high-agency units.

evidence.source: Nursing quality analyst, unit-level lag analysis across 18 inpatient units, Q1 2024-Q3 2026 (internal report, 2026-09)
evidence.text: Correlation between a unit's charge-plus-orientation shifts per charge-qualified RN in a quarter and the unit's RN resignation rate: same quarter r = 0.24; one quarter later r = 0.49; two quarters later r = 0.68; three quarters later r = 0.52. Correlation between a unit's resignation rate in a quarter and its agency share two quarters later: r = 0.63. All 18 units are on the same RN pay scale and the same differentials. The analyst notes: 'This is correlational and runs in both directions; it does not by itself establish cause.'

evidence.source: 4 West workload pilot evaluation (Director of Nursing Education, 2026-10-15), with matched-unit comparison from HRIS
evidence.text: From 2025-10-01, 4 West (32-bed medical unit, agency share 24%) received a 0.9 FTE nurse educator who took over all agency buddy orientation, and a cap of 3 charge shifts per RN per month, backfilled by two charge-qualified float RNs. Agency share on 4 West stayed at 22-24% throughout; pay, differentials and the unit manager (in post since 2022) were unchanged. Comparison units chosen before the pilot: 5 West (agency share 22%) and 6 East (25%), similar size and case mix, no pilot. Charge-plus-orientation shifts per charge-qualified RN, Q3 2026: 4 West 2.6; 5 West 5.9; 6 East 6.1. Share of staff scoring 'high' on the monthly emotional-exhaustion pulse item: 4 West 68% (Sep 2025) to 41% (Mar 2026); 5 West 66% to 70%; 6 East 64% to 67%. RN resignations per quarter, Q3 2025 / Q4 2025 / Q1 2026 / Q2 2026 / Q3 2026: 4 West 4 / 4 / 4 / 2 / 1; 5 West 4 / 5 / 5 / 6 / 6; 6 East 5 / 4 / 6 / 5 / 6. The evaluation notes that most Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 leavers on 4 West had handed in notice or accepted other offers before or shortly after the pilot began.

evidence.source: HR exit-interview summary, Jan 2025-Sep 2026 (HR Business Partner for Nursing, 2026-10-10)
evidence.text: Of 279 RN resignations in the period, 188 completed a structured exit interview. Primary reason given: workload, charge or precepting burden 49%; pay 17%; relocation or family 14%; scheduling 11%; other 9%. 63% of leavers had 2-8 years' tenure, the band from which most charge- and preceptor-qualified RNs are drawn; this band is 41% of the permanent RN workforce.

136 RN resignations Jan-Sep 2026; destination known for 98. St. Brennan's Hospital: 19 (all resigned Feb-Jun 2026). Travel or agency nursing: 27. Other hospitals or clinics: 22. Left bedside nursing or the profession: 30.

evidence.source: Regional healthcare compensation survey, RN base pay, 2024-2026 (state hospital association, published 2026-07)
evidence.text: Regional RN median base wage rose 9.4% in 2025 and 7.9% in 2026. Larchmere's RN scale rose 3.0% in each year. Larchmere's median RN base wage as a share of the regional median: 101% (Jan 2024), 95% (Jan 2025), 91% (Jan 2026).

evidence.source: Regional press coverage and St. Brennan's job postings (compiled by Larchmere Communications, 2026-10)
evidence.text: St. Brennan's Hospital, a 220-bed facility 18 miles from Larchmere, began advertising RN posts in October 2025 with a $20,000 sign-on bonus and opened on 2026-03-09. Its posted RN base scale is about 4% above the regional median.

evidence.source: CFO memo to the board finance committee, 'FY2027 RN recruitment incentive' (2026-10-06)
evidence.text: Proposes a $15,000 sign-on bonus for up to 80 external RN hires in FY2027 ($1.20M), with a 12-month clawback. To remain budget-neutral, it is funded by suspending the charge-nurse differential ($3.00/hour) and the preceptor differential ($2.00/hour) for FY2027 (estimated saving $1.31M). Each new external RN hire requires a 12-week preceptorship with a preceptor-qualified permanent RN.

evidence.source: HR evaluation of the 2025 sign-on bonus (HRIS and payroll, 2026-08)
evidence.text: A $7,500 sign-on bonus with a 12-month clawback ran for hires starting Jan-Jun 2025. External RN hires: 64 in Jan-Jun 2025 versus 52 in Jul-Dec 2024. Vacancy rate: 8.6% at 2024-12-31, 10.9% at 2025-06-30, 12.6% at 2025-12-31. Of the 64 bonus hires, 24 had left by month 15; 16 of the 24 left in months 12-15, after the clawback period ended. Preceptor shifts worked by permanent RNs rose 31% in Feb-Jul 2025 versus the prior six months.

evidence.source: Anonymous nursing staff survey (June 2026; n = 612 permanent RNs, 80% response)
evidence.text: 71% agree 'I am in charge or precepting more often than I can do safely'; 64% are considering leaving within 12 months (among charge-qualified respondents: 77%). Most frequent free-text theme (212 comments): orienting a new traveler every week or two while carrying a full assignment and charge. Pay was the theme of 74 comments.

evidence.source: Chair, Staff Nurse Practice Council, 6 East charge nurse (interview, 2026-10-30)
evidence.text: 'The differential is the only thing that acknowledges we run the unit and train every traveler. If it goes so that new hires can get fifteen thousand dollars, the charge-qualified nurses on my unit have told me they will drop their charge qualification or leave. Then who orients the bonus hires?'

evidence.source: Quality and Patient Safety department, falls with injury by unit, TTM to Sep 2026 (incident-reporting system, 2026-10-18)
evidence.text: Falls with injury per 1,000 patient-days: units with agency share above 20%: 0.71; units below 10%: 0.38. The high-agency units include 5 East (neuro step-down) and 7 North (step-down), which together have the highest fall rates (0.94 and 0.88). High-agency units also have a higher mean patient acuity index (1.42 vs 1.05) and a higher share of patients aged 75 or over (46% vs 29%). Director of Quality: 'We have not done a unit-month analysis that adjusts for acuity, census or patient age, and we do not record which nurse was assigned to the patient who fell.'

evidence.source: Director of Talent Acquisition (interview, 2026-10-28) and 7 North nurse manager (interview, 2026-10-30)
evidence.text: Director of Talent Acquisition: 'Median requisition-to-offer for RNs is 41 days, in line with what peers report; time-to-hire is not our problem.' 7 North nurse manager: 'I lose good candidates every month because someone else offers first.' The applicant tracking system does not record candidate withdrawals by stage or reason, and no comparison of Larchmere's offer timing with competitors has been made.

hypotheses.text: The tripling of agency spend is mainly a price effect: regional wage inflation pushed agency bill rates up, rather than the hospital buying many more agency hours.

A self-reinforcing loop is operating: vacancies drive agency use; because agency RNs cannot take charge or precept and require buddy orientation, those duties concentrate on permanent RNs, raising exhaustion and resignations, which create more vacancies.
The opening of St. Brennan's Hospital started the rise in Larchmere RN resignations.
Below-market base pay is the primary driver of Larchmere RN resignations.
Slow time-to-hire in Larchmere's recruitment process is a material constraint on filling RN vacancies.

edges.from: Agency share of a unit's RN hours
edges.to: Charge and buddy-orientation shifts per charge-qualified permanent RN

edges.from: Charge and orientation load on permanent RNs
edges.to: Permanent RN resignations, with a lag of roughly two quarters

edges.from: Agency share of a unit's RN hours

edges.to: Sustained reduction in the RN vacancy rate

actions.text: Adopt the proposed $15,000 sign-on bonus for external RN hires in FY2027, funded as in the CFO memo by suspending the charge-nurse and preceptor differentials.

Extend the 4 West model (dedicated educator for agency orientation plus a monthly charge-shift cap with float backfill) to the seven units above 20% agency share, tracking exhaustion scores and resignations at two and three quarters.
Sign a three-year recruitment process outsourcing contract for RN hiring to cut time-to-hire.
To reduce falls, bar agency RNs from 5 East and 7 North and cover the released hours with mandatory overtime from permanent staff.

Make agency-rate renegotiation the hospital's primary lever for bringing agency spend down by the end of 2027: at the January 2027 contract renewal, replace the uncapped wage-index escalator with a capped rate, using the lower framework vendor quotes as leverage.

evidenceRequests.text: RN applicant funnel by stage, with withdrawal timing and reasons (ATS and recruiter logs), 2025-2026
Unit-month falls with injury versus agency share, adjusted for acuity, census and patient age
Stay interviews with charge-qualified RNs on the seven high-agency units
St. Brennan's full published RN pay scale and sign-on terms
Line-item audit of agency invoices against timesheets
